Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajeev Sawhney,Raju Kumar Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Pachori,J.
Heard Sri Raju Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material on record.

The present second bail application has been filed on behalf of applicant Vinod Chauhan under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 72 of 2021 for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, registered at Police Station Sector 39 Noida, District Gautam Budh Nagar, during pendency of the trial, after rejecting the first bail application of the applicant by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court of this Court, vide order dated 14.11.2022.

sentences.text: Present applicant filed an Special Leave Petition before Supreme Court against the rejection of first bail application, wherein while dismissing S.L.P., the Supreme Court observed that if the trial is not completed within a period of nine months from the order dated 27.3.2023, petitioner would be at liberty to renew his prayer for bail before the trial court.
About 13 months have been elapsed from the date of passing of order dated 27.3.2023 by the Supreme Court and examination-in-chief of PW-1 has been recorded in the trial court only.

Brief facts of the case are that first information report dated 20.2.2021 has been lodged by one Satyapal Singh against the applicant and other 97 named and three unknown persons, on the basis of an application u/s 156(3) of Cr.P.C., alleging that present applicant sold out property of the first informant and executed 36 different sale deeds on the basis of false and forged registered power of attorney of the first informant in favour of other co-accused.
As per pre-summoning evidence, a registered power of attorney bearing Registration No. 1731, year 2019, which is paper no. 87 of paper book, has been collected.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that in earlier bail application, it has not been taken the plea that there is no allegation with regard to preparing false and forged power of attorney by impersonating the first informant against the applicant.

It is further submitted that there is no pre-summoning evidence with regard to preparing forged power of attorney, however, which is a registered document, wherein photograph and thumb impression of the informant is affixed.

It is further submitted that all the sale consideration of 36 sale deeds have been transferred in the account of the company- M/s S.S. Associate and Director of the company namely Sumit has been granted interim protection by the Division Bench of this Court in Crl. Misc. Writ Petition No. 1057 of 2022, vide order dated 14.2.2022.

entities.text: Crl. Misc. Writ Petition No. 1057 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It is further submitted that investigation of other co-accused persons is pending since 20.2.2021.
He has next argued that the applicant has criminal history of one case.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 27.12.2021.

Learned counsel for the applicant has relied upon the judgments of Apex Court in Ash Mohammad Vs. Shiv Raj Singh @ Lalla Babu and another, (2012) 9 SCC 446 and Prabhakar Tiwari Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2020) 11 SCC 648 wherein the Apex Court has observed that pendency of other criminal cases against the accused may itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the innocence of the applicant cannot be adjudged at pre trial stage, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence.
In case the applicant is released on bail, he will again indulge in similar activities and will misuse the liberty of bail.

sentences.text: It is well settled position of law that bail is the rule and committal to jail is an exception and refusal of bail is a restriction on the personal liberty of the individual guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution [Vide State of Rajasthan vs. Balchand @ Baliay (1977) 4 SCC 308, Gudikanti Narasimhulu And Ors Vs. Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Andhra Pradesh, AIR 1978 SC 429 and Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Another, (2021) 10 SCC 773].

sentences.text: No material or circumstances has been brought to the notice of this Court with regard to tampering of evidence or intimidating of witnesses in previous criminal history.

Keeping in mind, larger mandate of Article 21 of the constitution of India, the nature of accusations,
the nature of evidence in support thereof, the severity of punishment which conviction will entail,
the character of the accused-applicant, circumstances which are peculiar to the accused, reasonable possibility of securing the presence of the accused at the trial, reasonable apprehension of the witnesses being tampered with, the larger interest of the public/ State and other circumstances, but without expressing any opinion on the merits, I am of the view that it is a fit case for grant of bail.
Hence, present second bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant Vinod Chauhan be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat, or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in the trial court.
(v) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
(vi) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

If in the opinion of the trial court that absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then Vinod Chauhan vs State Of U.P. on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150782703/

The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously in accordance with law after the release of the applicant, if there is no other legal impediment.

It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The trial court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything said in this order.

The party shall file computer generated copy of such order downloaded from the official website of High Court Allahabad, self attested by the applicant alongwith a self attested identity proof of the said person (preferably Aadhar Card) mentioning the mobile number to which the said Aadhar Card is linked.
